name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Jim Jordan is a well-funded, high-profile incumbent with $6M on hand
Democratic challenger raised only ~$13K with negligible cash
Prediction markets price Jordan at ~95% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Jordan: a deeply Republican seat, a powerful incumbent with a massive financial advantage, and a Democratic opponent who has raised almost nothing. Markets price this race as effectively decided, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or an unexpected Jordan scandal could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Jordan seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans about 21 points Republican at the baseline. He is one of the House's most prominent conservatives and has built a commanding campaign operation, with roughly $4.8 million raised this cycle and $6 million in the bank. No outside groups are spending against him.

His opponents face steep odds. Democrat Joshua Kolasinski has raised about $13,000 with under $500 on hand, and independent Tracey Tackett shows no measurable fundraising. No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets give Jordan roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The seat is rated Safe R on fundamentals alone.
